newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-SPORTING CRISTAL, CRUZEIRO REACH LIBERTADORES CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPORTING CRISTAL, CRUZEIRO REACH LIBERTADORES CUP FINAL.

text.p: Sporting Cristal became the first Peruvian side to reach the Libertadores Cup final in 25 years on Wednesday as they overcame Racing Club of Argentina in their semifinal.
Cristal's opponents will be former champions Cruzeiro of Brazil, who beat Chileans Colo Colo on penalties in Santiago after their tie had ended 3-3 on aggregate.
The Santiago game began half an hour late because of torrential rain and was marred by unsavoury scenes at the end when Colo Colo players attacked Cruzeiro substitute Da Silva.

There was also a strange second-half incident when a fan threw an object at Cruzeiro striker Elivelton as he was about to take a corner. Elivelton threw the object back and was promptly sent off by the referee.
Colo Colo's Brazilian midfielder Emerson was also shown the red card for two bookable offences.

Peru have only been represented once before in the final, when Lima club Universitario lost out to Independiente of Argentina in 1972. They line-up with Ecuador, Venezuela and Bolivia as the countries never to have claimed the trophy.
Sporting, whose line-up includes Ghanaian midfielder Prince Amoako, earned their final place in style as they beat 1967 champions Racing 4-1 before a 45,000 crowd to go through 6-4 on aggregate.
Luis Bonnet, who scored a crucial late goal in the first leg in Buenos Aires, fired the Peruvians in front after five minutes.
Marcelo Delgado headed Racing level after 35 minutes but Cristal regained the initiative when Julio Rivera scored three minutes before the break.
Bonnet turned into the scourge of Racing when he scored again in the 51st minute before Nolberto Solano settled the tie with a rasping drive 18 minutes from time.
A hat-trick by former Chilean international Ivo Basay was not enough for Colo Colo, the only Chilean team to have won the competition, in Santiago.
Trailing 1-0 from the first leg, Colo Colo levelled the tie when Basay scored with a 20th minute header only for Marcelo to volley Cruzeiro level on the night nine minutes later.

Basay converted two penalties in four minutes at the start of the second half to put the Chileans ahead on aggregate but a 64th minute goal by Cleison, who beat the Colo Colo defence to a loose ball, sent a dramatic tie to penalties.

Basay then undid his good work by firing Colo Colo's first effort at Cruzeiro goalkeeper Dida, who went on to save the Chileans' next shot. Marcelo Espina then missed another attempt as Colo Colo's nerves broke.
